content.text:
**Short answer: Under international law and by the position of Ukraine and most of the international community, Crimea is part of Ukraine, not Russia.** Russia has controlled and administered Crimea since it annexed it in 2014, but that annexation is widely not recognized.

In March 2014, the UN General Assembly adopted Resolution 68/262 affirming Ukraine’s territorial integrity and calling on states not to recognize any change in Crimea’s status after the referendum held there. ([press.un.org](https://press.un.org/en/2014/ga11493.doc.htm?utm_source=openai)) The U.S. and many allies describe Crimea as **occupied Ukrainian territory** and call for Russia to return control to Ukraine. ([2021-2025.state.gov](https://2021-2025.state.gov/crimea-is-ukraine/?utm_source=openai))

So the distinction is:

- **De facto control:** Russia controls Crimea.
- **De jure/legal international status:** Crimea is generally recognized as part of Ukraine.
